transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… thank you, Doctor. I’m here because there have been these… incidents at work, I guess. I keep hearing people talking about me, like through the conference room walls, or sometimes from my phone even when it’s turned off.

It sounds like board members or staff saying I’m ruining the company. I know that probably sounds… dramatic, and I don’t want to make too much of it, but it feels very clear in the moment. Sometimes I answer them before I realize no one else heard anything. Is that… the kind of thing I should be telling you?
Can you tell me how long you've been experiencing these voices and the feeling that people are talking about you—did this start days ago, weeks ago, or longer?

I think… it’s been about three months. Not every second or anything, and I kept hoping it was just stress or me misunderstanding things, but the voices from the walls or my phone started around then. Is that the kind of timeframe you mean?
Have you been using any alcohol, marijuana, or other recreational drugs in the past few months?

I… I don’t think so, not anything like that. I mean, I’m not trying to hide anything from you—I just don’t really have much to report there. I haven’t noticed any drug use being part of this, if that’s what you’re asking.

Over these past three months, have you also noticed periods of feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or losing interest in things—or, on the other hand, feeling unusually elated, energetic, or needing much less sleep?

I’m not sure I’d say that, no. I mean… I’ve been stressed and preoccupied, definitely, but I haven’t noticed a clear stretch where I was unusually happy or full of energy, or anything like that. And I don’t think I’ve been really hopeless either.

I may not be explaining it perfectly—if there’s a specific kind of mood change you mean, I can try to think about it that way.

Since these experiences began, have you noticed any changes in your ability to function at work or in your daily routine—for example, trouble concentrating, meeting deadlines, or taking care of everyday tasks?

Yes… I mean, I’d like to say I’m still managing, but honestly it hasn’t been very good. At work I’m not reliably keeping up the way I used to. I run a division, and lately the decisions that should be basic for me feel… hard to stay on top of, and I think senior staff have been quietly stepping in and taking over things I used to handle myself.

At home too, I guess I’ve been leaving things unfinished, or not starting them. My husband has had to take on most of the household stuff. I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve completely fallen apart, but… it has affected things. Is that the kind of functioning you mean?

Before these voices started three months ago, did you notice any earlier changes—like withdrawing from people, having unusual beliefs, or a decline in your functioning—that might have started even earlier, say four to six months ago or more?

Yes… I suppose if I’m being honest, it wasn’t just suddenly three months ago. I’ve been trying not to make too much of it, because I was under a lot of pressure, but things had been… building for quite a while.

It probably started around the company expansion, when I was put in charge of the new arts-and-commerce division. That was maybe two years and four months ago. I told myself it was just the workload and the adjustment, but looking back, that’s when things started to feel different. Does that make sense as an answer?

During that earlier period, say from around the time of the expansion, did you also experience unusual beliefs or perceptions—like sensing people were watching or talking about you, or hearing things—or was it mainly a decline in your motivation and functioning without those specific experiences?

The more specific things… the voices, I mean, from the walls or sometimes from my phone, that’s really been more like the last three months.

Before that, I think I was struggling and not doing as well, but I don’t want to overstate it. I don’t remember hearing things like that back when the expansion first started. Is that the distinction you’re asking about?

Since that decline began around two years ago, has there been a continuous period—lasting at least six months—where you noticed both the reduced functioning and, more recently, the voices, without significant breaks where you felt completely back to your normal self?

I think… yes, in the sense that it hasn’t really gone back to how I used to be. It’s been building since the company expansion, when I was put in charge of the new arts-and-commerce division—about two years and four months ago now.

I kept telling myself I was just adjusting, or that anyone would struggle with that much responsibility, but I don’t think there was a stretch where I felt completely like my old self again. Is that what you mean by continuous?
